catalog.note: Deep diagnostics for problems normal metrics and thresholds can’t see. These analyses fetch long histories and run heavier models, so they run as background jobs — start one, keep working, review the report when it lands.
catalog.toolsSub: Pick a tool, set its scope, and run it as a job.

list.emptyAll: No findings — nothing stood out in this scope and window.

anomaly.note: Baseline-relative deviations across every collected series. Each finding is scored by how far and how unusually it left its learned envelope.

correlation.note: Metric pairs that moved together inside the window. Each finding is a relationship between two series, scored by how tightly they track — what actually co-moved, not just what alarmed.

capacity.note: Utilization projected forward by trend to estimate when each resource runs out. Sorted soonest-first — the runway shows the projection arriving at the 100% ceiling.

flap.note: Nodes whose reachability keeps bouncing. Rate is what matters — a dozen flaps in an hour is an outage, a dozen over a week is noise — so findings rank by flaps per hour.

event_storm.note: Nodes whose passive-event rate surged past their own learned baseline. What matters is the multiple, not the raw count — 400 events in 5 minutes is routine for a busy aggregation switch and alarming for an access port.

severity_shift.note: Nodes whose syslog mix skewed toward error-or-worse against their own baseline — a quiet degradation signal. Volume is shown alongside: +40 pp out of 12 events is noise, out of 4,000 it is an incident.

rule_gap.note: High-volume events that no rule matched, clustered by signature. This is a work queue rather than a diagnosis — each row is traffic you are receiving but not acting on, so the fix is to write a rule for it.

auth_probe.note: Authentication failures clustered by the source doing the authenticating — brute force, or a misconfigured NMS hammering SNMP/SSH. The source is the subject here; the node is the target.

event_flap.note: The same event rule raising and clearing over and over — linkDown/linkUp thrash and BGP session churn that reachability flap analysis can't see. Group by rule to find one rule thrashing fleet-wide.
event_flap.balanceTitle: {{fires}} fired vs {{clears}} cleared — a long fired side means raised and never resolved

traffic_anomaly.note: Nodes whose flow volume surged past their own baseline — DDoS, saturation, a runaway backup, or exfiltration. Ranked by the multiple over baseline, so a busy uplink and a quiet access port are comparable.

talker_shift.note: Addresses that became dominant talkers this window without appearing in the previous one — a new heavy source, a rogue device, or the start of an exfil. The rank it entered at is the signal.

phases.compare: Comparing talkers against the previous window…

new_destination.note: Traffic to a destination that wasn't there in the baseline window. A new external AS can mean C2 or exfiltration; a new port usually means a new service or a scan. The two are listed separately because they are different findings with different severity ceilings.
new_destination.noAs: No new destination AS in this window.
new_destination.noPorts: No new destination ports in this window.

phases.compare: Comparing destinations against the previous window…

anomaly.name: Anomaly Detection
anomaly.desc: Learns each metric’s own baseline and flags statistically significant deviations — slow drifts and odd shapes that fixed thresholds never trip.
anomaly.reveal: spikes · level shifts · stuck counters · seasonality breaks

correlation.name: Event Correlation
correlation.desc: Cross-correlates metrics inside a window to surface what actually moved together — not just what alarmed.

capacity.name: Capacity Forecast
capacity.desc: Projects resource utilization forward by trend to estimate when each will hit exhaustion.

flap.name: Flap Analysis
flap.desc: Scans reachability state churn to surface nodes that bounce up/down and quietly drop sessions.

event_storm.name: Event Storm
event_storm.desc: Baselines each node's passive-event rate and flags a sudden surge — boot loops, interface churn, or a chatty misconfiguration.

event_flap.name: Event Flap
event_flap.desc: Counts repeated fire↔clear cycles of the same event rule — linkDown/linkUp thrash and BGP session churn the reachability flap analysis can't see.

severity_shift.name: Severity Shift
severity_shift.desc: Detects a node whose syslog severity mix skews toward error/critical versus its baseline — a quiet degradation signal.

rule_gap.name: Rule Gap
rule_gap.desc: Clusters high-volume unmatched events by signature so you can see which traps or messages deserve an event rule.

auth_probe.name: Auth Probe
auth_probe.desc: Clusters authentication-failure traps and syslog by source to surface brute-force attempts or a misconfigured NMS.

traffic_anomaly.name: Traffic Anomaly
traffic_anomaly.desc: Baselines each node's flow volume and flags a spike — DDoS, saturation, a runaway backup, or exfiltration.

talker_shift.name: Talker Shift
talker_shift.desc: Compares the top talkers this window to the previous one to surface a newly dominant host — a new heavy source or rogue device.

new_destination.name: New Destination
new_destination.scope: dst AS / port · window vs window
new_destination.desc: Flags traffic to a destination AS or port absent from the baseline window — a new external destination, service, or scan target.

flow_scan.name: Scan Detection
flow_scan.desc: Finds a source contacting an abnormal number of distinct destinations or ports — horizontal/vertical scans and worm spread.

saturation.name: Link Saturation
saturation.desc: Surfaces a single conversation dominating a busy node's traffic and attaches the node's current interface throughput as context.

incident_correlate.name: Incident Correlate
incident_correlate.desc: Assembles a cross-signal timeline for a node — a metric anomaly, passive events, and the dominant flow — when they coincide, for root-cause triage.
